review: 7:1–7:2 מָה־אָשִׁיב לַאדֹנָי / עַל־כָּל־טוּבוֹ — Psalm 116:12 verbatim (מָה־אֶשִּׁיב לַיהוָה כָּל־תַּגְמוּלוֹהִי עָלָי); the Arabic مَاذَا لِرَبِّي أَرْدُدُ is that verse.
1:2 שִׁחְרְרֵנִי — 'He set me free'; the Arabic فَكَّنِي is 'He loosed me', and the piel of שחרר is the biblical verb for freeing a slave (Lev 19:20).
2:4 נִכְמַר עָלַי — 'grew tender over me' (Gen 43:30, נִכְמְרוּ רַחֲמָיו); the Arabic قَلْبُهُ قَدْ رَقَّ لِي is that idiom, and the niphal of כמר is its Hebrew form.
5:3 בִּגְדֵי נֵצַח — 'garments of victory', for ثَوْبَ الظَّفَر; the Arabic is 'the robe of triumph', and נֵצַח in the sense of enduring victory is the closest single noun.
4:2 כֵּן — 'yes', standing for the Arabic نَعَمْ; the affirmation is kept as its own word because the line needs the beat.
